analysis.title: Weekly Headings (Investment Strategy), October 23, 2026
key_insights: Next week is the busiest of 3Q26 earnings season: 172 S&P 500 companies representing about 37% of S&P 500 market cap report. Catalysts over the next two weeks also include the FOMC meeting, the Treasury Quarterly Refunding Announcement (Nov 4) and the midterm elections (Nov 3).

Markets price only a 10% probability of a Fed rate hike at next Wednesday's FOMC, down from about 70% after last month's hike. Raymond James says the meeting could be more 'live' under the Warsh-led Fed than pricing implies, given inflation above 2% for more than five years and oil near $100.

Raymond James base case is one more hike in December followed by a prolonged pause. A hawkish dissent in October would not be surprising, since four FOMC members penciled in two more hikes by year-end in the September dot plot.

3Q26 S&P 500 earnings are up about 29% YoY so far, the fifth straight quarter of double-digit EPS growth and the longest streak since 2018. 82% of companies beat EPS estimates versus a 10-year average of 77%.

Hyperscalers Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft are the focus next week, with cloud revenue, capex guidance and free cash flow in view. Hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending is expected to exceed $1T in 2027. The results test the earnings growth underpinning the firm's 8,450 12-month S&P 500 target.
Visa, Mastercard, Hilton and Starbucks will give a read on consumer resilience, and UPS and FedEx on broader economic activity.

The Nov 4 Treasury refunding could trim longer-maturity issuance and possibly eliminate new 20-year bonds. Less long-end supply could temporarily support bond prices, but total borrowing needs are unchanged and issuance would shift to bills or shorter maturities, raising refinancing risk. Growth and inflation remain the more durable drivers of rates.

Democrats have an advantage heading into the midterms. With Trump's approval near a record low of 39%, the Washington Policy team sees Democrats well placed to win the House, Senate control a toss-up, and a Democratic sweep the most likely scenario. The S&P 500 has gained about 15% on average in the 12 months after midterms and was positive every time since 1942.

Market leadership reversed from September to October. Tech and Communication Services are each down more than 4% month-to-date, and the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index has beaten the cap-weighted index by nearly 4%, its strongest monthly outperformance since February.

Raymond James stays constructive on Tech and expects it to regain leadership. 2027 Tech EPS estimates are up about 2% this month, Tech EPS growth is expected to outpace the S&P 500 through at least 2Q28, and Tech valuations relative to the S&P 500 are near the lowest since 2020.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell below 5% for the first time in a month, with a 17 bp one-day drop, the largest since August 2024. It is on track for a 32 bp monthly decline, the steepest since February 2025, after seven months of rising yields.
IG credit spreads are +7 bps on the month to 87 bps. IG Tech spreads widened 15 bps to 102 bps, their widest since June 2023 and the largest gap to the broader index on record.

US-Iran conflict is a key geopolitical risk. Expanding US military preparations and coordination with Israel raise concern about a resumption of strikes after the Nov 3 elections. Iran has threatened retaliation against energy sites and data centers and AI facilities in the region.

France's 10-year yield topped 5% for the first time since 2002. France's deficit is set to exceed 5% of GDP for a fourth year, and Raymond James expects yields to drift higher if deficits stay at current levels.

Economic data: NAHB builder sentiment fell to 29, the lowest since June 2012, and 43% of builders cut prices, the highest share since COVID. Initial jobless claims stayed below 200k for a sixth week. NRF projects holiday spending above $1T, up 4.2% YoY.

sector_views.rationale: Share price weakness is not matched by weaker fundamentals. 2027 EPS estimates are up about 2% this month, EPS growth should outpace the S&P 500 through 2Q28, and relative valuation is near the lowest since 2020.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS up about 29% YoY with about a quarter of the index reported (reported results so far), the fifth straight quarter of double-digit growth. 82% of companies have beaten EPS estimates versus a 10-year average of 77%.

Week of Oct 26: 172 companies, about 37% of S&P 500 market cap, report. Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft report, with cloud revenue, capex guidance and free cash flow in focus. Visa, Mastercard, Hilton, Starbucks, UPS and FedEx also report (previews, no estimates given).

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price a 10% hike probability and Williams and Jefferson signal little urgency to tighten, so a hold with a brief press conference is the base case.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation above 2% for more than five years, oil near $100 and four officials projecting two more hikes make a hawkish dissent or surprise possible.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hawkish dissent or an October hike would invalidate the hold-and-pause view.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech 2027 EPS estimates are up about 2% this month, growth outpaces the S&P 500 through 2Q28, and relative valuations are near the lowest since 2020.
tension_points.bear_case: Building AI spending and financing concerns, and wider IG Tech credit spreads, have driven Tech and Comm Services down more than 4% month-to-date.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak cloud revenue or capex guidance from Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft would undermine the Tech recovery call.
